name: Bø 1999
question: How do supervised pelvic floor muscle training, vaginal electrical stimulation, and weighted vaginal cones compare with no active treatment for women with genuine stress incontinence?

design.population: Women with clinically and urodynamically confirmed genuine stress urinary incontinence from five centers in southeast Norway.
design.description: Multicenter, assessor-blinded, four-arm randomized superiority trial

verdictNote: Supervised training improved pad-test leakage and subjective severity more than the other strategies.
takeaway: In women with genuine stress incontinence, supervised pelvic floor muscle training reduced standardized pad-test leakage and patient-reported severity more than vaginal electrical stimulation, weighted vaginal cones, or no active treatment after six months.

reports.label: Six-month primary report
reports.citation: Bø K, Talseth T, Holme I. "Single blind, randomised controlled trial of pelvic floor exercises, electrical stimulation, vaginal cones, and no treatment in management of genuine stress incontinence in women." *BMJ.* 1999;318(7182):487-493. doi:10.1136/bmj.318.7182.487

results.measure: Mean change in leakage, baseline to six months (g); global four-group comparison
results.note: Kruskal-Wallis global comparison; a negative change means less leakage. Treated-participant analysis (25, 25, 27, and 30 women, respectively).

results.measure: Condition rated unproblematic at six months
results.note: P value compares change from baseline in the exercise group with the other groups; five-category self-rating.
results.locator: Results, Subjective cure; Methods, Subjective assessment

results.measure: Standardized pad-test leakage ≤2 g at six months
Women wanting treatment beyond their assigned strategy after six months
results.note: Question asked at the end of assigned treatment.

harms.label: Reported treatment adverse effects

values.stim: 2 women reported smarting, tenderness, or bleeding

harms.locator: Results, Adverse effects and treatment tolerance
harms.note: Event counts are reported without an adverse-event analysis denominator; women may have reported more than one symptom.

harms.label: Withdrawal attributed to pain or bleeding
harms.note: Other withdrawals included motivation, travel, unrelated circumstances, and use of other treatments.

delivery.label: Assigned treatment protocols
delivery.value: PFMT: 8–12 near-maximal contractions three times daily plus a weekly 45-minute therapist-led class; electrical stimulation: MS 106 Twin vaginal stimulation at 50 Hz for 30 minutes daily; cones: Mabella 20, 40, and 70 g weights for 20 minutes daily; control: continence guard offered.

delivery.label: Pad-test protocol
delivery.value: After catheter emptying, bladder filled with 200 mL saline; 30 seconds running in place and 30 seconds jumping jacks; pad weight change measured.
delivery.locator: Methods, Main outcome measures, Pad test with standardised bladder volume

delivery.label: Statistical plan
delivery.value: Global Kruskal-Wallis comparison with P <0.05 as the significance threshold; primary treated-participant analysis and intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis carrying baseline values forward for missing measurements.

delivery.label: Trial flow and treatment adherence
delivery.value: 122 randomized (PFMT 29; stimulation 32; cones 29; control 32); 107 in treated-participant efficacy analysis (25; 25; 27; 30). Mean adherence: PFMT 93% (SE 1.5%); stimulation 75% (SE 2.8%); cones 78% (SE 4.4%).
